patch_description: The previous best program (2.36) used a true triangular-lattice layout with row spacing g = s*sqrt(3)/2 (equilateral local geometry) and an exact LP for radii. The current program regressed (2.02) by using uniform row/column spacing, which creates non-equilateral gaps. I restore the triangular-lattice constructor, vectorize the LP constraint assembly with numpy broadcasting + scipy sparse matrices (per the identified bottleneck), and add a short randomized hill-climb on center positions: each step perturbs a few centers slightly, re-solves the LP, and keeps improvements. Vectorizing the LP makes each step cheap enough to fit many refinement iterations in the runtime budget, pushing sum of radii toward the 2.635 target.
